notes: Chapter title. Latin 'CAPVT PRIMVM.' = English 'CHAPTER I.' Both are annotated as body lines (not headers) in their respective JSON, so this is a normal body-to-body alignment.
Chapter subtitle. Latin 'In quo Controuerſia hæc omnis in ſuas particulares quæſtiones diſtribuitur.' = English 'WHEREIN THIS WHOLE CONTROVERSY IS DISTRIBUTED INTO ITS PARTICULAR QUESTIONS.'

Foundation sentence quoting John 5:39. Latin embeds Greek + own Latin paraphrase: 'Ἐρευνᾶτε τὰς γραφὰς, Scrutamini Scripturas.' Parker Society renders Greek verbatim + English in caps: 'Ἐρευνᾶτε τὰς γραφὰς, SEARCH THE SCRIPTURES.' Note: 'Fuerat enim' at end of Latin l0007 belongs to the NEXT sentence (unit u004); annotator put it on this line due to typesetting.
Christ commended to Jews by John the Baptist. Latin l0007 has 'Fuerat enim' tail; English l0007 has 'Christ had been commended to the Jews by' tail — these belong here, not in u003.
Christ claims three greater testimonies than John's: works, Father, scriptures. English l0011 starts mid-line 'Yet Christ declares…'.
Jews esteem scriptures; Christ approves and exhorts more zeal. 'Et quidem de Scripturis…' / 'The Jews, indeed, thought honourably…'. English uses 'hath' construction — register signal for the prompt.
Christ exhorts to search not just read; like searching for buried treasure. 'Hortatur enim…' / 'For he exhorts them…'.
Search the WHOLE of scripture, not selected parts. 'Et quando Chriſtus ſine exceptione…' / 'Now since Christ hath bid us…'. English l0026 contains 'hath' — register signal.
All parts of scripture testify to Christ. 'Omnes enim Chriſto non obſcurum teſtimonium dicunt.' / 'All parts give plain testimony to Christ.'
Papists and we both prize scriptures; no controversy that they should be searched. Sentence spans page boundary in both languages — IMPORTANT cross-page case for the runner.
The actual controversy is the manner of searching, who should search, and what counts as scripture. 'verum de modo…' / 'But concerning the due manner of searching them…'.
Divides controversy into six questions. 'Quam vt perſpicuè & certa methodo tractemus…' / 'In order to effect this clearly and methodically…'.

Question 1: number of canonical books. 'Iubemur Scripturas ſcrutari…Ergo hæc erit prima quæſtio, De numero Canonicorum librorum Scripturæ.' / 'We are commanded to search…The first question therefore shall be, Of the number of the canonical books of scripture.'

Question 2: translations and vernacular liturgy. 'Iubemur Scripturas ſcrutari…Ergo ſecunda queſtio erit, De Scripturarum verſionibus, ſacrisque vernaculis.' / 'We are commanded to search the scriptures: and therefore…The second question therefore shall be, Of versions of the scripture and sacred rites in the vulgar tongue.'

Question 3: scripture's authority — intrinsic vs. derived from church. End of Latin c1_ch1 in this corpus (p0031_body_l0033 'ex Eccleſiæ teſtimonio.'). English c1_ch1 continues onto questions 4–6 in p0042; out of scope for this exercise — see plan.md §4.
